app.deploy.description: Activate an exact reviewed application release on its approved host. Activation uses the existing application identity and data custody; publishing source alone does not deploy it.

app.upgrade.description: Change an application to an exact reviewed release. The plan must disclose availability and data/schema consequences; returning to the previous executable does not by itself reverse data changes.

app.repair.description: Re-establish the already accepted application configuration. Repair does not silently adopt newer source, replace data from a backup, or resolve a different interrupted operation.

app.undeploy.description: Make the application inactive by removing its managed execution while retaining persistent data and its recovery obligations. This is not permission to delete application data or backups.

app.backup.description: Capture and publish an application recovery checkpoint using its declared data procedures. A successful capture is distinct from evidence that restoration has been tested.

app.backup-check.description: Check the selected application backup material through its configured capability. Integrity checking does not itself demonstrate a successful isolated restore drill.

app.restart.description: Restart only the named components of the accepted application release. Persistent data remains under its existing custody; normal application writes may resume.

app.maintenance-run.description: Run one task resolved from the receiver's accepted application release with its exact approved scope. The effective minimum role is the higher of app.maintenance-run and the expanded app.backup, app.backup-check or app.drill action. Those built-in tasks cannot select a hook. The native-maintenance branch selects one declared hook and requires administrator regardless of its hook role; it cannot lower the permission floor of restore, drill or other owner work. The receiver checks this role and current scoped authority for manual and scheduled execution. A task declaration or schedule cannot delegate administrator authority. The plan explains data changes or downtime; a task name does not authorize arbitrary host commands.

app.secrets-adopt.description: Adopt the exact completed provider-neutral publication receipt under current local authorization. Verify its accepted secret-source binding, catalogue, entry, immutable version and protected material custody before changing consumers. Publication success alone does not establish adoption or application health.

app.restore.description: Restore application data from the explicitly selected checkpoint. The plan must identify replacement scope, possible loss of later writes and production admission; this is not a synonym for restarting or repairing configuration.

app.drill.description: Test restoration of the selected checkpoint in isolation from production writers. A drill supplies recovery evidence and does not activate the restored copy as the production application.

app.recover.description: Resolve the named interrupted or quarantined operation using an explicit disposition and any selected checkpoint. Preserve confirmed effects and reconcile uncertainty; recovery is not a fresh attempt with forgotten request identity. origin is null for an operation of the current epoch; historical recovery requires the exact retained Operation reference and verified custody under a new current-epoch Plan. The old operation is immutable and retains its original authority identity.

app.cleanup.description: Reclaim only the exact candidates in the reviewed inventory under the current protected-reference checks. Rebuildability or inactivity alone does not authorize removal of data, backups or accepted recovery material.

app.retire.description: End management of this application only with explicit retention and custody evidence. Retirement is separate from temporary inactivity and does not imply erasing retained data.

recovery_basis.description: Exact reviewed recovery basis. A checkpoint retains the selected preserved data closure. A release basis is permitted only when the independently loaded accepted application source has no app-owned dataset with preserve recovery; it pins the accepted release and its reconstruction inputs. It covers data-free and rebuild-only applications without inventing a captured dataset. It does not waive external custody, reconstruction verification or destination admission.

app.relocate.description: Move the same application identity to the selected host through a fenced ownership handoff under the exact recovery basis. The receiving owner checks the basis against independently loaded accepted source and custody; a caller cannot reclassify preserved data as rebuildable or data-free. Source and destination must not become concurrent production writers. A release basis changes neither fencing nor permissions and cannot authorize deletion; changing placement text alone does not move the application.

host.apply.description: Apply an exact reviewed host source snapshot to its managed scope while preserving unmanaged state. Review compares the accepted baseline, observed live state and proposed state for every affected scope. A live administrator edit requires an explicit preserve, capture or overwrite disposition bound into the plan; source precedence alone cannot authorize replacement. The executor must revalidate the reviewed live preimage before mutation and stop for renewed review if it changed. This changes accepted host configuration; publishing a snapshot or capturing a proposal does not apply it.

host.runtime-install.description: Install the exact reviewed management-tool release through the protected host owner. Tool installation is separate from application deployment and must preserve accepted work and independent recovery.

host.reboot.description: Reboot the selected host after admitting the exact disruption and recovery plan for its affected work. A dropped connection is not evidence that reboot completed.

host.sleep.description: Put the selected host to sleep after its affected work is made safe. Sleeping is a power state, not evidence of an unhealthy machine or failed application.

host.wake.description: Ask an approved relay to wake the named host. Dispatching a wake request does not prove that the host is awake, reachable or ready to serve applications.

host.capture-changes.description: Capture selected live host changes against the named source base as a reviewable source proposal with an exact live preimage. Capturing a proposal neither publishes it nor adopts it as accepted configuration, and grants no permission to overwrite a later live edit. A host.apply capture disposition must retain and verify custody of its exact reviewed preimage before replacement.

host.source-update.description: Update the named managed source checkout to an exact commit with its custody checks. Updating source does not apply host policy, activate an application or discard unpublished human work.

host.secrets-adopt.description: Adopt the exact completed provider-neutral publication receipt under current local authorization. Verify its accepted secret-source binding, catalogue, entry, immutable version and protected material custody before changing consumers. Publication success alone does not establish adoption or application health.

host.recover.description: Resolve the named interrupted host operation with an explicit disposition, retaining confirmed outcomes and unresolved custody. Do not replace the original request merely because its reply was lost. origin is null for an operation of the current epoch; historical recovery requires the exact retained Operation reference and verified custody under a new current-epoch Plan. The old operation is immutable and retains its original authority identity.

host.retire.description: Retire only the named host resources after their retention and replacement custody is established. This does not authorize bulk deletion of unrelated or unmanaged resources.

source.publish.description: Publish the exact reviewed source proposal against its named base through the authorized repository publisher. Publication changes source history; it does not activate that source on any host or application.

dns.reconcile.description: Apply the exact reviewed DNS changeset conditionally within the granted scope. Preserve unowned records and distinguish provider acceptance from independently observed effective DNS state.

publisher.publish.description: Publish this exact protected secret-candidate to the accepted secret-source instance, entry, consumer and immutable version under the reviewed catalogue digest. Independently compare the typed predecessor before publication and retain provider-specific evidence under its installed pinned schema. The candidate is held by the publishing owner. Publication alone neither rotates an issuer value nor confirms consumer adoption. Backend bundle, key-value and versioned-store details are opaque to this core action. evidence_schema is the independently installed provider publication-evidence schema pinned during review; output cannot select another schema.

publisher.recover.description: Reconcile the exact interrupted publication using its retained receipt, publication identity and candidate digest. Retained source binding, entry, consumer, catalogue, predecessor and protected candidate cannot change. Recovery cannot invent a replacement destination or immutable version; a changed candidate requires fresh review. A lost reply is not proof of nonpublication.

recovery.publish.description: Publish the selected recovery capture under its existing custody and completeness checks. Published source recovery material is not proof that application data or external accounts can be restored.

backend.check.description: Check the selected backup backend through its enrolled implementation. This does not initialize an unknown repository, restore an application or demonstrate a restore drill.

backend.prune.description: Remove only backup material authorized by the exact retention evidence, the current owner-accepted retention policy and current protected references. Revalidate policy identity, holds, accepted work and recovery roots at deletion. A backup adapter, generic adapter action or cleanup plan cannot weaken an accepted keep-local policy or delete the sole viable recovery copy. A policy relaxation requires a separately reviewed owner-accepted change.

adapter_release.description: Exact immutable artifact digest used as the approved Installation key and InstanceReference.installation_digest. The receiver separately verifies the descriptor, configuration, grants and scoped instance; this artifact pin alone supplies no authority.

adapter.execute.description: Execute the exact declared adapter action and input through a receiving-owner-approved artifact, configuration and scope. Resolve the actual native targets and mutation facets and enforce the same controlling owner, accepted binding, admission, holds, retention and recovery obligations as the corresponding typed operation. Generic dispatch grants no alternate authority. An executor subordinate to a runtime controller must use that controller's durable attempt and admission path; an adapter identity or scope label alone cannot authorize it. This is an advanced capability boundary, not a general shell or source-controlled enrollment mechanism. The receiving owner independently resolves the approved selected method and requires its result schema identity to match result_schema. Planning binds that schema; a caller cannot select a more permissive result contract.

backend.enroll.description: Explicitly attach a known backup repository or initialize the selected new one under the reviewed mode. Unknown initialization outcomes require reconciliation rather than another initialization attempt.

operation.recover.description: Reconcile one exact original Operation through its receiving local owner and independently installed native recovery procedure. The reviewed resource must equal the original Operation resource, including adapter, publisher, source, DNS and backend resources. Resolve the original action, retained invocation, protected inputs and effects from owner custody; do not choose a new executor or infer no effect from a timeout. Planning explicitly refuses unsupported native reconciliation. Current scoped administrator approval, positive native cessation/fencing and retained holds are required. The original Operation remains immutable; this new request has its own Plan and identity. origin is null only for a current-epoch Operation; historical work requires exact retained reference and current-authority custody.
